QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_43

question.text: Under Regulation 20, the Investment Manager is prohibited from providing advisory services for investment in securities of investee companies where the AIF managed by it invests. What is the EXCEPTION to this prohibition?

answer.text: Advisory may be provided to investors of a Co-investment scheme or clients of a Co-investment Portfolio Manager (per PMS Regulations 2020).
No exception; the prohibition is absolute.
Advisory may be provided to any LP of the AIF on a reciprocal basis.
Advisory may be provided if the Manager obtains 51% LP consent.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per workbook pp.281 and 246 (Regulation 20): 'The Investment Manager shall not provide advisory services to any investor OTHER THAN the investors of a Co-investment scheme or clients of a Co-investment Portfolio Manager as specified in the SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations, 2020, for investment in securities of investee companies where the AIF managed by it makes an investment.' Option A captures that exception and is the keyed correct answer. The Trap: Absolute prohibition (Option B) is wrong — the co-investment exception exists. Reciprocal advisory (Option C) and 51% LP consent (Option D) are invented workarounds. Note: Removed the register-a-PMS-arm structuring pro-tip and the Cross-Exam Context paragraph, since those structuring tactics go beyond the Regulation 20 carve-out supported on pp.281 and 246.
